text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your normal readings so far. Since we cannot rule out central causes yet, do you have any history of stroke, diabetes, or high blood pressure? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). With normal audiometry, negative central imaging, and no hearing loss, the most likely cause of your sudden vertigo is displaced otoconia in the semicircular canals.
